root/code-induced-converse-structure.title: Code-induced converse structure
root/code-induced-converse-structure.summary: Study exact necessary conditions inherited from deterministic private-message codes, including dependence balance, fixed-coordinate encoder structure, compatible rate rows, and the unresolved support-reduction problem.

root/entropy-copy-relaxation-limits.title: Entropy/copy relaxation limits and channel-specific constraints
root/entropy-copy-relaxation-limits.summary: Determine the limits of coarse entropy/copy refinements of code-induced converse constraints and pursue exact binary-posterior or other channel-specific consistency constraints that are not captured by universal entropy geometry.

root/relaxed-uv-functional-tensorization.title: Separately relaxed UV scalar tensorization
root/relaxed-uv-functional-tensorization.summary: Study product additivity, receiver-skew symmetry, and exact evaluation of the separately relaxed scalar UV sum-rate functionals, without extending conclusions to the full UV region, common joint-(U,V) optimization, GK functional, broader converse systems, or capacity.

root/result/finite-block-code-induced-ba.title: Finite-block code-induced dependence balance and compatible rate rows
root/result/finite-block-code-induced-ba.summary:
This is the finite-block component of an attributed, independently audited port of the consecutive accepted Yukon artifacts `upper-dependence-balance` and `upper-entropy-nogo`, which together form one dependency-complete structural result. Let A and B be independent uniform private messages of sizes N₁,N₂≥2, encoded deterministically over n uses of a finite-alphabet memoryless broadcast channel. Receiver Y estimates A with average error p₁ and receiver Z estimates B with average error p₂. Define Fⱼ=h₂(pⱼ)+pⱼ log₂(Nⱼ−1), δⱼ=Fⱼ/n, and Sᵢ=(Yⁱ⁻¹,Zᵢ₊₁ⁿ). Then exactly

Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ [I(A;B∣Sᵢ,Yᵢ)−I(A;B∣Sᵢ,Zᵢ)] = I(A;B∣Yⁿ)−I(A;B∣Zⁿ).

Both endpoints are nonnegative, while Fano bounds them by F₁ and F₂, respectively. With independent uniform time T and U=A, V=B, W=S_T, X=X_T, Y=Y_T, Z=Z_T, every such code induces

|I(U;V∣W,T,Y)−I(U;V∣W,T,Z)| ≤ max{δ₁,δ₂}.

The complete induced law retains the fixed coordinate map:

p(t,u,v,w,x,y,z)=(1/n)p_U(u)p_V(v)p(w∣u,v,t) 1{x=f_t(u,v)}P_{YZ∣X}(y,z∣x).

In particular, U⊥V, T⊥(U,V), X=f_T(U,V), and realized W cannot select another encoder map after (u,v,t) are fixed. With Rⱼ=(1/n)log₂Nⱼ, the same variables satisfy

R₁≤I(U,W;Y∣T)+δ₁,
R₂≤I(V,W;Z∣T)+δ₂,
R₁+R₂≤I(U,W;Y∣T)+I(X;Z∣U,W,T)+δ₁+δ₂,
R₁+R₂≤I(V,W;Z∣T)+I(X;Y∣V,W,T)+δ₁+δ₂.

This is an exact sequence-level necessary condition. The message alphabets and W may grow with blocklength, so it is not by itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region and does not establish a new capacity upper bound.

root/result/entropy-copy-no-go.title: Exact entropy/copy no-go theorem for the stated coarse BSSC relaxation
root/result/entropy-copy-no-go.summary:
At uniform input, put h=h₂(1/4), c=h−1/2, and r=h−3/4. Consider the coarse entropy relaxation imposing: (i) the complete seven nonempty entropies of the common-noise BSSC coupling, namely H(X)=1, H(Y)=H(Z)=h, H(X,Y)=H(X,Z)=H(Y,Z)=3/2, and H(X,Y,Z)=2; (ii) message/time independence, deterministic encoding, the fixed-map equality, the memoryless Markov equality, and exact dependence balance; (iii) every conditional BEC identity I(L;Y,Z∣K)=(1/2)I(L;X∣K) for disjoint subtuples L,K⊆{U,V,W,T}, L nonempty; and (iv) the two sharp scalar BSSC posterior-support inequalities with right side r. There is an actual finite entropic point satisfying all these constraints for which both direct sum branches equal

2h₂(1/4)−5/4 = 0.3725562489182657… .

Consequently, adding any collection of universally valid finite-variable information inequalities, including unknown non-Shannon inequalities, cannot lower this relaxation below that value. Nor can any finite sequence of standard copy-lemma extensions: each copy step can be realized by conditional resampling of the finite witness while preserving its original marginal and objective. The witness is deliberately not a binary BSSC distribution: X is a tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components. Exact binary-posterior or other channel-specific consistency constraints exclude it and remain viable. The theorem obstructs only the stated coarse entropy/copy relaxation and finite sequences of standard copy-lemma extensions; it does not establish a new capacity upper bound.

root/proof/finite-block-balance-and-rate.title: Telescope, Fano, fixed-map factorization, and conditioned Csiszár proof
root/proof/finite-block-balance-and-rate.summary: Set Dᵢ=I(A;B∣Yⁱ,Zᵢ₊₁ⁿ) for 0≤i≤n. The ith balance summand is exactly Dᵢ−Dᵢ₋₁, so summation gives the claimed endpoint telescope without a channel inequality. Separate Fano bounds control D_n by F₁ and D₀ by F₂. After uniform time sharing, memorylessness and deterministic encoding give the fixed-coordinate induced-law factorization because, conditional on (A,B,T), the current input is fixed and the current output is independent of the past/future outputs in W. The individual rate rows follow from Fano and forward or reverse chain rules. The two sum-rate rows follow from conditioned Csiszár sum identities; the uncancelled remainders are respectively ΣᵢI(Yⁱ⁻¹;Yᵢ) and ΣᵢI(Zᵢ₊₁ⁿ;Zᵢ), hence nonnegative.

root/proof/entropy-counterfeit-witness.title: Posterior-support calculation and finite entropic counterfeit construction
root/proof/entropy-counterfeit-witness.summary: For g(q)=I_Z(q)−I_Y(q), direct differentiation gives g″(q)=(2q−1)/(ln(2)q(1−q)(1+q)(2−q)), so g is concave through 1/2 and convex thereafter. The exact identities g(1/5)=(8/5)r and g′(1/5)=−2r make 2r(1−q) a global upper support. A posterior mixture of mass 5/8 at 1/5 and 3/8 at 1 has mean 1/2 and support value r; reflection gives the other direction. The finite witness uses mutually independent binary components C,A,B1c,B2c,Eu,Ev,Ny,Nz with respective entropies 2r, 1−h, r, 7/4−2h, 1/2−r, r, 1/2, 1/2, and tuple variables U=(C,A,B2c,Eu), V=(B1c,Ev), X=(C,A,B1c,B2c,Eu,Ev), Y=(C,A,Ny), Z=(C,B1c,B2c,Nz), with W,T constant. Component-set intersections verify the complete base entropy vector, structural equalities, all conditional BEC identities, exact dependence balance, both support rows, and both objective branches. Because this is an actual finite distribution, every universally valid finite-variable information inequality holds. Conditional resampling realizes each finite standard copy-lemma extension while preserving the original marginal and objective.

root/tool/exact-entropy-witness-checker.title: Exact affine-in-h entropy-witness checker
root/tool/exact-entropy-witness-checker.summary: A reproducible standard-library Python checker represents every component entropy as an exact rational affine expression a+bh with h=h₂(1/4). Using weighted component unions and intersections rather than floating-point arithmetic, it checks positivity from 3/4<h<7/8, the complete base entropy vector and structural equalities, both zero-valued dependence-balance sides, all 65 disjoint-subtuple conditional BEC identities, both sharp support rows, and both objective branches at 2h₂(1/4)−5/4. It reports successful exact audits for the affine-in-h construction, the 65 BEC identities, dependence balance, support rows, and both branches.

root/question/safe-support-reduction.title: Safe support reduction for code-induced laws
root/question/safe-support-reduction.summary: Is there a cardinality or compactness reduction that simultaneously preserves U⊥V, T⊥(U,V), X=f_T(U,V), I(X;W∣U,V,T)=0, both sides of the code-induced dependence-balance constraint, and all four compatible rate rows? The accepted result supplies no such reduction.

root/question/binary-posterior-penalty.title: Exact penalty from jointly consistent binary BSSC posteriors
root/question/binary-posterior-penalty.summary: Find an exact inequality for jointly consistent binary BSSC posterior refinements that supplies a strict penalty absent from universal entropy geometry. Exact binary-posterior or other channel-specific consistency constraints can exclude the accepted tuple-valued counterfeit and remain viable.

root/result/separately-relaxed-uv-tensor.title: Product tensorization of separately relaxed UV scalar functionals
root/result/separately-relaxed-uv-tensor.summary: For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel W and input law p, define t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)−I_p(X;Z), let 𝔠[f](p) be the upper concave envelope of f at p, and put A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+𝔠[−t_W](p), D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+𝔠[t_W](p), B_avg(W)=sup_p(A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2, and B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. For finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, the averaged separately-relaxed UV sum-rate functional defined in this contribution is exactly additive under products. On a receiver-skew channel the branchwise functional equals the averaged functional, and the same equality and additivity hold for every finite product of receiver-skew channels. Consequently, for the half-skew BSSC P and every integer n >= 1, both functionals on P^{times n} equal n(2 h_2(1/4) - 5/4) bits. This is a theorem only about the two separately-relaxed scalar UV functionals, not about tensorization of the full UV region, a common joint-(U,V) optimization, the GK functional, or the capacity itself. The BSSC specialization relies on the previously accepted sharp scalar BSSC posterior-support inequality and contact identity.

root/proof/separately-relaxed-uv-product.title: Concave-envelope product decomposition and receiver-skew symmetrization
root/proof/separately-relaxed-uv-product.summary: For a product channel, opposite-order mutual-information expansions and the Csiszár sum identity decompose the conditional receiver-information difference into factorwise terms. Applying this to every posterior ensemble bounds the upper concave envelopes of t and −t by the sums of their factor envelopes, including for correlated product inputs and auxiliaries joint across factors. Output entropy subadditivity supplies the corresponding A and D upper bounds. Product input laws and independent products of factor posterior ensembles give the reverse inequalities, proving exact additivity of B_avg without an attainment assumption. For a receiver-skew involution S, relabeling gives A(Sp)=D(p) and D(Sp)=A(p); concavity at (p+Sp)/2 then proves B_br=B_avg and permits restriction to invariant input laws. Product involutions extend this equality and additivity to finite products. For the half-skew BSSC, the invariant binary input is uniform, and the previously accepted sharp posterior-support inequality together with its attaining posterior mixture evaluates both envelopes there as h_2(1/4)−3/4, yielding n(2h_2(1/4)−5/4).

root/tool/uv-bssc-specialization-checker.title: High-precision half-skew BSSC relaxed-UV specialization checker
root/tool/uv-bssc-specialization-checker.summary: A reproducible standard-library Python script evaluates the BSSC mutual-information formulas at 90-decimal precision, checks the support contact at q=4/5, the attaining posterior mixture with masses 5/8 and 3/8, the receiver-skew channel relations, and the normalized value 2h_2(1/4)−5/4. It corroborates the exact BSSC specialization; the universal product and symmetry theorem rests on the analytic proof.
